title: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV / CLV) Modeling
description: Mathematical estimation of the net present economic value generated across an entity's relationship lifespan.
conditions: Evaluating customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback and unit economics
Segmentation of customers into lifetime value tiers for resource allocation
recommended_methods: Simple historical LTV = Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) * Gross Margin % / Churn Rate
Buy 'Til You Die (BTYD / BG-NBD) probabilistic models for non-contractual transactional data
Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) net present value projection
selection_rules: In contractual subscription models, use ARPU * Margin / Churn Rate with annual discount rate
In non-contractual retail models, use BG-NBD model to predict future transaction counts and Gamma-Gamma for spend
Benchmark LTV to CAC ratio: healthy unit economics typically target LTV:CAC >= 3.0
limitations: Simple LTV formulas assume constant churn rate, which fails because churn rate drops sharply as customer tenure increases
Overestimating LTV can lead to catastrophic overspending on marketing acquisition channels
source: Fader and Hardie (2005) Counting Your Customers the Easy Way
